complexity.notes: The deque swap fixes the O(n) pop(0) from the previous version, and iterating list(edges) instead of edges[::-1] is a safe copy either way. The remaining cost drivers are the full edge-list copy and rescan per dequeued vertex, plus linear edges.remove / in vertices / vertices.remove list scans; membership tests on vertices would at least be O(1) with a set, though the rescan dominates. O(n + m) is achievable by ||building an adjacency list once up front (or using union-find) with a visited set||.
complexity.summary: Counts components via BFS, but instead of an adjacency structure it iterates a fresh copy of the entire edge list on every dequeue, removing incident edges and enqueuing any neighbors still in the unvisited-vertices list.
